claims.text: Temperature-dependent local lattice distortions govern the unresolved stress–strain and thermoelastic behavior of HfNbTaTiZr.
Local lattice distortions arise from atomic-size mismatch among Hf, Nb, Ta, Ti, and Zr.
Dynamic short-range order allows local lattice distortions to modulate mechanical strength.
Dynamic short-range order allows local lattice distortions to modulate elastic properties.
Local lattice distortions intensify at 600–800 °C.
Intensified lattice distortions at 600–800 °C cause hardening.
Intensified lattice distortions at 600–800 °C cause anomalous elastic moduli.
At 1250 °C, increased atomic mobility reduces lattice-distortion effects.
Reduced lattice-distortion effects at 1250 °C result in creep-dominated behavior.
At intermediate temperatures, stabilized distortions impede dislocation motion.
At high temperatures, relaxation of distortions enables creep.
Aging at 600–800 °C will increase microhardness relative to the as-cast, unaged alloy.
Aging at 600–800 °C will produce a non-monotonic temperature dependence of elastic modulus.
Aging at 600–800 °C will reduce the thermal expansion coefficient relative to the as-cast, unaged alloy.
At 1250 °C, mechanical strength will decrease.
At 1250 °C, elastic modulus will approach the value expected for a random solid solution.
At 1250 °C, thermal expansion will match rule-of-mixtures predictions.
The as-cast, unaged HfNbTaTiZr baseline exhibits typical solid-solution behavior at room temperature and 1250 °C.
Homogenization and solution treatment remove residual stresses from the initial material.
Alloys with less atomic-size mismatch may not exhibit the proposed effects.

contradictions.description: The initial material is called as-cast while also being homogenized and solution-treated, whereas the baseline and comparison are described as as-cast and unaged. These are distinct processing states, so the stated baseline is internally ambiguous and may not isolate aging.
